world.bio: I teach antenatal and postnatal yoga at a community centre in Stockport, three evenings and one Saturday morning a week. I came to it through my own pregnancies, did my teacher training in Manchester, and have been running classes for about six years. Most of what I know about the medical side I have read myself, so I am careful with my wording. Outside work I am training for a spring half marathon.
skills_assets: Antenatal and postnatal yoga teacher training, 85-hour course plus a pregnancy specialism module
Regular classes at a community centre in Stockport: Tuesday and Thursday evenings, Saturday mornings, about 14 women per class
A folder of handouts: breathing, pelvic floor, positions for late pregnancy, gentle postnatal recovery
A mailing list of roughly 120 past and present participants
Bolsters, blocks, birth balls and a stack of mats stored in a cupboard at the centre
First aid certificate, renewed this year

projects.name: New term handouts
projects.text: I rewrite my handouts before every term. This autumn I am reworking the breathing and positions sheets. After a partner complained that one of my breathing tips contradicted what their midwife said, I want these checked by someone with clinical experience before term starts in January. At the moment they are based on books, my teacher training and my own experience, which does not feel like enough any more.

projects.name: Class numbers and the centre budget
projects.text: The centre told me in the summer that there is no money to expand to a second room, so I am capped at fourteen. I would love to run a mums-and-babies class on Friday mornings but there is nowhere for it. I wrote a proposal in July and have not heard back.

projects.name: Half marathon training
projects.text: Training plan for the Manchester half in April. Currently on three runs a week, long run on Sundays along the Mersey. I am slower than last year because of the cold I never really shook off.

notes.text: Tuesday class went fine, thirteen women. One of the newer ones, maybe 30 weeks, looked very tired and I wondered if I should have said something. I have no training for that. I told her to rest in child's pose and she smiled and said she was fine. I still thought about her all the way home on the bus.

Long run along the Mersey, 14 km, felt terrible. My knees hurt and the headwind never stopped. I ate a flapjack at the end sitting on a bench and watched a dog chase a stick into the river. It came back with a different stick.

Mum rang again at 7am to ask what day it was. She sounded annoyed that I told her. She was diagnosed in the spring, early dementia, and the doctor said it would be slow. It is not slow enough. I did the dishes with the radio on very loud so I would not cry in front of the kids.

Broadband has been dropping out again, third time this week. I spent forty minutes on hold with the provider and was told to turn it off and on again. I am going to compare providers this weekend. There is a cheaper one with a better review on the forum my neighbour uses.

Got a message after Thursday's class from a partner of one of the women. Polite, but he said the breathing tip I gave about slow exhale through the mouth was not what their midwife had told them. I looked it up and my version was not wrong exactly, but it was not the same advice either. I felt hot in the face. This is exactly what I worry about, that I say something with total confidence and it is wrong for one person.

Spent the evening going through my handouts, line by line. I found three places where I give advice I cannot actually source. They are things I picked up in training or from other teachers. Everyone says them, but nobody I know has checked. I am a yoga teacher, not a midwife, and the women trust me more than I deserve.
Tried a new loaf recipe, forgot the salt. It looked wonderful and tasted of nothing. The kids ate it with a lot of butter and said it was fine, which is the worst kind of review.

Saturday class, ten women plus two babies who slept through everything. Afterwards one of the mums said she cried for the first time in three weeks during the final relaxation. I think that is the thing I do well. Not the poses. The ten minutes of quiet.

Mum had a bad day. She called my brother 'Dad' and then got upset when he corrected her. I drove over after work and made tea. She watched the TV with the sound off. We did not say much. On the way home I stopped in a layby and cried for ten minutes.

The centre manager said the room will be shut for a week in November for new heating. Which means I will lose a week of classes and some of the women will complain. I should email them early. Added it to the list.

messages.text:
Pat: Hannah, just to say the Thursday room might be tied up in November for the boiler. Will confirm.
Me: Thanks Pat. Is there any chance of the small hall as a backup?
Pat: Don't hold your breath. The budget's tight.

Partner: Hi, I wanted to mention that what you said about the breathing seemed to contradict what the midwife told us at the appointment on Monday. Not trying to cause trouble, just thought you'd want to know.
Me: Thank you for telling me, I really appreciate it. I'll look into it and update the handout.

Dan: Mum wouldn't take her tablets this morning.
Me: I'll come Sunday.
Dan: We need to talk about the care options.
Me: I know.

Kat: Sunday long run? I can do 16.
Me: I'll try. My knee has been grumbling.
Kat: Ice it. And please don't wear those old trainers again.

Jess: Hannah, baby arrived! 8lb 2. Thank you for everything, I used the breathing in labour and it really helped.
Me: Congratulations!! So happy for you.

Tom: What do you fancy for tea?
Me: Anything. Not bread.
Tom: Pasta then. The kids have been asking.

relations.about: Early dementia diagnosed in spring; lives alone ten minutes away with a carer twice a week
Lives in Leeds, helps by phone, argues about care options
Works in logistics, takes the kids to school most mornings

constraints: No budget for paying anyone for a review, I would need to find someone willing to look at things for free or a small fee
Evenings are taken by classes Tuesday and Thursday; Saturday morning too
I will not give medical advice, only movement and breathing guidance
Weekdays are the best time for any meeting during the day
sensitive: Feels like an impostor about the medical side of her teaching
Money is tight; teaching income about £900 a month
Worried about her mother and about her own risk of dementia
